content: 1. Maraviroc and Maraviroc/Apomorphine: Co-administration of maraviroc and apomorphine may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs. This combination also raises the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Close monitoring is advised, and caution should be exercised. 2. Maraviroc and Aprepitant: Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Maraviroc and Aripiprazole: Maraviroc may increase the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 4. Maraviroc and Armodafinil: Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Maraviroc and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Maraviroc and Asenapine: Co-administration may increase the effects of both drugs through mechanisms not fully understood. This combination may also increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Maraviroc and Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily. Monitor closely. 8. Maraviroc and Atenolol: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Maraviroc and Atidarsagene Autotemcel: Antiretroviral medications, including maraviroc, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Avoid antiretroviral therapy for at least one month before cell mobilization and during the expected duration of drug elimination. Monitor closely. 10. Maraviroc and Atomoxetine: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of atomoxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Maraviroc and Atorvastatin: Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Maraviroc and Avanafil: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Maraviroc and Azilsartan: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Maraviroc and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: This combination increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Maraviroc and Benazepril: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Maraviroc and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Hydromorphone, a metabolite of hydrocodone, may contribute to the total analgesic effect. Monitor closely. 17. Maraviroc and Berotralstat: Berotralstat increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Monitor or titrate the dose of P-gp substrates if co-administered. 18. Maraviroc and Betaxolol: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Maraviroc and Betibeglogene Autotemcel: Avoid antiretroviral therapy for at least one month before mobilization and until all cycles of apheresis are completed, as antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. 20. Maraviroc and Bexarotene: Bexarotene decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Maraviroc and Bisoprolol: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Maraviroc and Bosentan: Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Maraviroc and Budesonide: Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Maraviroc and Bumetanide: Co-administration may increase the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Maraviroc and Butabarbital: Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Maraviroc and Butalbital: Butalbital decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Maraviroc and Candesartan: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Maraviroc and Captopril: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Maraviroc and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Maraviroc and Carvedilol: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Maraviroc and Cenobamate: Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed and monitor closely. 32. Maraviroc and Ceritinib: Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Maraviroc and Chloramphenicol: Chloramphenicol increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Adjust the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily and monitor closely. 34. Maraviroc and Chlorthalidone: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Maraviroc and Cimetidine: Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Maraviroc and Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily and monitor closely. 37. Maraviroc and Clevipidine: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Maraviroc and Clomipramine: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Maraviroc and Clotrimazole: Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Maraviroc and Cobicistat: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily and monitor closely. 41. Maraviroc and Codeine: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of codeine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 42. Maraviroc and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily and monitor closely. 43. Maraviroc and Conjugated Estrogens: Conjugated estrogens increase the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Maraviroc and Cortisone: Cortisone decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Maraviroc and Crizotinib: Crizotinib increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs metabolized by CYP3A. 46. Maraviroc and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Maraviroc and Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 48. Maraviroc and Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Maraviroc and Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 50. Maraviroc and Danazol: Danazol increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Maraviroc and Danicopan: Danicopan increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 52. Maraviroc and Darifenacin: Darifenacin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Maraviroc and Darunavir: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily and monitor closely. 54. Maraviroc and Dasatinib: Dasatinib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Maraviroc and Deferasirox: Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Maraviroc and Desipramine: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of desipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Maraviroc and Dexamethasone: Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Maraviroc and Dexfenfluramine: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of dexfenfluramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 59. Maraviroc and Dextroamphetamine: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 60. Maraviroc and Dextromethorphan: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of dextromethorphan by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 61. Maraviroc and DHEA (Herbal): DHEA increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Maraviroc and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: This combination increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Maraviroc and Diltiazem: Diltiazem increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Maraviroc and Donepezil: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of donepezil by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 65. Maraviroc and Doxazosin: Co-administration may lead to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the effects of both drugs and raising the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Maraviroc and Doxepin: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 67. Maraviroc and Dronedarone: Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Maraviroc and Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 69. Maraviroc and Duloxetine: Maraviroc increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Maraviroc and Duvelisib: Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates and monitor for signs of toxicity. 71. Maraviroc and Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Maraviroc and Elagolix: Elagolix increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 73. Maraviroc and Eliglustat: Eliglustat increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
